patches.old: The worst case remains O(b^d) nodes. For a uniform tree with perfect ordering, the ideal minimum leaf count is b^ceil(d/2) + b^floor(d/2) − 1; for even depth this has the familiar O(b^(d/2)) growth [23]. Neither bound is an elapsed-time prediction, because node costs and branching vary. Memory remains depth-first: O(d) stack frames and up to O(db) live move entries, in addition to the board. Equality cutoffs preserve the root value, although tie selection and visited-node counts can depend on traversal order.

patches.old: A concrete race illustrates the mechanism. Suppose request A is searching round 8. The person invokes a New game before A finishes. The controller increments its token, clears state and changes the round. Even if A's response was already queued, its captured token no longer matches. The promise resolution cannot insert A's move into the new board. Meanwhile, cancelPending rejects pending transport promises and terminates the old Worker, so future requests construct a new one. The token guard and resource cancellation address different parts of the race [2], [6].
